mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's recent shots_on_target FOR is elevated relative to its long-run mean AND Team B's recent shots AGAINST is elevated relative to its long-run mean. Measure whether the cross-product of these two deviations is associated with Team A goals FOR beyond what each deviation predicts independently.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A goals FOR rises more steeply when both Team A's shot quality (shots_on_target/shots ratio) is above its long-run level AND the opponent's shots-allowed is above its long-run level, compared to when only one condition holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has risen in recent matches while its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target / shots) has also improved recently, whereas Team B concedes markedly more shots in recent matches than its long-run average. The joint condition of one team's improving shot quality alongside the opponent's recent defensive deterioration in shot-volume-allowed may produce a non-additive relationship with goals scored that neither observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables from two different perspectives (Team A's own shot quality trend AND Team B's defensive shot-volume trend) simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band, nor to a simple home/away or recent-vs-long-run split on a single metric.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's possession FOR is below a threshold (e.g. below competition mean of 50%) AND Team B's possession FOR is also below its own long-run mean. Measure whether corner_kicks FOR Team A and shots FOR Team A jointly behave differently in this dual-low-possession regime versus when possession is more balanced.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams are simultaneously below their respective possession baselines, Team A's corner_kicks FOR and shots FOR show a different joint distribution than when possession is more one-sided, suggesting a non-linear interaction between the two teams' possession deficits.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A operates with a persistent below-average possession share (long-run ~44.8%, recent ~42.8%) while Team B has recently dropped below its own long-run possession average. When both teams are simultaneously in a low-possession regime, the joint possession deficit may be associated with a distinct corner-kick and shots pattern compared to matches where only one team is possession-deficient.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This conditions on two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (Team A's own possession level AND Team B's possession level), and examines the joint relationship with two output observables. It cannot be reduced to a single observable split by one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's offsides FOR is simultaneously elevated above its long-run mean AND Team B's offsides AGAINST is elevated above its long-run mean. Measure whether Team A's goals FOR is associated with this joint elevation differently than when only one offside dimension is elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A goals FOR rises when both Team A's offsides FOR and Team B's offsides AGAINST are jointly above their respective long-run means, consistent with a high-line defensive regime by Team B that creates more behind-the-line opportunities alongside more offside traps.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides FOR has spiked sharply in recent matches (long-run ~1.48, recent ~3.2) while Team B's offsides AGAINST has also spiked recently (long-run ~1.10, recent ~2.6). The joint elevation of both Team A's offensive line-breaking attempts and Team B's defensive line exposure may interact with Team A's goals FOR in a non-additive way — high offsides on both sides simultaneously may indicate a high-line defensive setup by Team B that creates both more offsides traps and more goal opportunities.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables from asymmetric perspectives (Team A's offensive offsides production AND Team B's defensive offsides concession) and their combined association with a third observable (goals). It requires two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously and is not reducible to any single-observable split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the within-match half structure: compare first-half vs second-half goal production for Team A FOR against Team B's first-half vs second-half goals AGAINST. Measure whether the joint second-half skew of both Team A's attacking output and Team B's defensive vulnerability produces a compounding effect on second-half goals, and whether this is further associated with elevated second-half card activity (cards_2h).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goals in matches involving Team A (home) and Team B (away) are elevated relative to first-half goals, and this elevation is associated with higher cards_2h, consistent with a late-game intensity regime driven by the joint half-level asymmetry of both teams.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goal production (long-run 0.586 per match) exceeds its first-half production (0.557), while Team B concedes more goals in the second half (0.757) than the first half (0.614). The asymmetry between Team A's half-level goal distribution FOR and Team B's half-level goal distribution AGAINST — both favouring the second half — may jointly amplify second-half goal activity beyond what either team's half-split alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This uses within-match half-level resolution for two teams simultaneously across two distinct observables (goals and cards_2h), conditioning on the joint half-skew of both Team A's attacking and Team B's defensive profiles. It is not a single observable split by one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's yellow_cards FOR is below its long-run mean AND Team B's yellow_cards FOR is above its long-run mean simultaneously. Within this asymmetric disciplinary regime, measure whether corner_kicks AGAINST Team A (i.e. FOR Team B) and second-half cards (cards_2h) are jointly elevated relative to matches where the disciplinary asymmetry is reversed or absent.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A is in a low-yellow-card regime and Team B is in a high-yellow-card regime simultaneously, corner_kicks FOR Team B and cards_2h are jointly elevated, consistent with Team B pressing more aggressively and generating both more set-piece opportunities and more disciplinary events.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's yellow cards FOR have declined sharply in recent matches (long-run ~2.36, recent ~1.6) while Team B's yellow cards FOR have risen recently (long-run ~2.34, recent ~2.6), and Team B's fouls FOR have declined recently (long-run ~12.39, recent ~10.6) while Team A's fouls AGAINST have also declined recently (long-run ~12.24, recent ~11.0). The joint divergence in disciplinary and foul profiles — one team becoming less aggressive while the other becomes more so — may interact with corner-kick production in the second half in a way not captured by either team's disciplinary profile alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This conditions on two distinct observables from asymmetric perspectives across both teams (Team A's yellow_cards FOR declining AND Team B's yellow_cards FOR rising) and examines their joint association with two further observables (corner_kicks and cards_2h). It requires simultaneous conditioning on two opponent-descriptor dimensions and involves an asymmetric cross-team relationship.
